description: Phase 1 MVP: Read cadence/speed data from the indoor bike's reed switch (2-pin connector, 1 pulse/rev) via IO35 and display it on the ESP32 2.8" ILI9341 screen. Wiring: reed switch → IO35 (10K pull-up to 3.3V) + GND. The ESP32-32E display board is both the microcontroller and the screen.

userStories.title: Probe and identify bike signal
userStories.story: As a builder, I want to probe the 2-pin connector with a multimeter so I can determine the signal type (reed switch, hall effect, or other) and voltage levels.
acceptance: Document the signal type (digital pulse, analog, etc.)
Measure voltage range when pedaling vs idle
Determine if a pull-up or pull-down resistor is needed
Identify the pulse-per-revolution count (likely 1)
userStories.notes: Reed switch confirmed. 1 pulse per revolution. No polarity — either wire to either pin.

userStories.title: Identify available ESP32 GPIO pin
userStories.story: As a builder, I want to identify which GPIO pin on the ESP32-32E display board I can use for the bike sensor input, given that most pins are used by the display, touch, SD card, and other onboard peripherals.
acceptance: Map out all GPIO usage on the specific board
Confirm IO35 (input-only) or IO27 are available
Test the chosen pin with a simple digitalRead sketch
Document wiring plan
userStories.notes: IO35 (input-only) selected. 10K pull-up to 3.3V. Test script at firmware/test/test_reed_switch.cpp.

userStories.title: Wire bike sensor to ESP32
userStories.story: As a builder, I want to physically connect the bike's 2-pin connector to the ESP32 GPIO so the microcontroller can read pedal pulses.
acceptance: Solder or connect wires from 2-pin connector to ESP32 GPIO + GND
Add pull-up resistor if needed (10K typical for reed switch)
Verify clean signal with serial output (no excessive bounce)
Add basic debounce in software if needed
userStories.notes: Wiring: reed switch wire 1 → IO35, wire 2 → GND, 10K pull-up from IO35 to 3.3V. Hardware assumed working.

userStories.title: Implement pulse counter firmware
userStories.story: As a rider, I want the ESP32 to count pulses from the bike sensor so it can calculate my pedaling cadence in real-time.
acceptance: Use hardware interrupt on the sensor GPIO pin
Count pulses and calculate RPM from pulse intervals
Handle edge cases: very slow pedaling, stopped, very fast pedaling
Debounce logic to avoid false counts from reed switch bounce
Serial output shows accurate RPM matching actual pedal speed
userStories.notes: Interrupt-driven pulse counter on IO35 with 50ms debounce, 3s timeout for stopped detection, RPM clamping (10-200), and 4-sample rolling average smoothing. Serial output at 2Hz. Sketch: firmware/pulse_counter/pulse_counter.ino

userStories.title: Calculate speed and distance
userStories.story: As a rider, I want to see my estimated speed and total distance so I can track my workout progress.
acceptance: Convert RPM to speed using configurable wheel circumference
Accumulate distance over the session
Display in sensible units (km/h or mph, km or miles — configurable)
Handle the indoor-bike-to-road-equivalent conversion reasonably

userStories.title: Set up Arduino CLI project and display Hello World
userStories.story: As a developer, I want a working arduino-cli build setup so firmware compiles and uploads to the ESP32-32E display board.
acceptance: Arduino sketch in firmware/<name>/<name>.ino compiles with arduino-cli
TFT_eSPI configured for ILI9341 with correct SPI pin mapping for this board
Compiles and uploads to the ESP32-32E display board via /dev/cu.usbmodem2101
Basic 'Hello World' renders on the 2.8" screen

userStories.title: Display dashboard UI v1
userStories.story: As a rider, I want to see a clean dashboard on the 2.8" screen showing my current RPM, speed, distance, and elapsed time so I can monitor my ride at a glance while pedaling.
acceptance: 240x320 layout with large, readable numbers
Shows: RPM (cadence), speed, distance, elapsed time
Updates in real-time (at least 2x per second for RPM)
Readable from typical bike riding position (~arm's length)
Dark background with high-contrast text for readability

userStories.title: Auto-detect session start and stop
userStories.story: As a rider, I want the session to start automatically when I begin pedaling and stop after a period of inactivity, so I don't need to press any buttons.
acceptance: Session starts on first detected pulse
Session pauses after 30 seconds of no pulses
Session ends after 2 minutes of no pulses
Elapsed time only counts active pedaling time (excludes pauses)
Clear visual indicator of session state (active, paused, ended)

userStories.title: Log session data to SD card
userStories.story: As a rider, I want my session data saved to the SD card so I can review past rides and track progress over time.
acceptance: Session summary written to SD card as CSV on session end
Fields: date, start_time, duration, distance, avg_rpm, max_rpm, avg_speed, max_speed
Raw data log option: timestamped RPM readings (for future analysis)
File naming: YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM.csv
Graceful handling if SD card is missing or full
